documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. 61 now. No complaints. Working full time, talking about cutting back in a couple of years. No palpitations; cardiology in the fall kept everything the same. Warfarin through their clinic, no bleeding. No cough or exertional breathlessness. RA quiet.
PHQ-2 0.
Exam: BMI 28. Eyes, ears, mouth normal. Neck, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear to the bases. Abdomen soft. Legs: no edema, calves equal. Joints without synovitis. Skin, no suspicious lesions.
A/P
- HTN: in range today, upper end. Will watch.
- PAF on amiodarone + warfarin (cardiology). TSH today, LFTs in CMP.
- Seropositive RA on MTX, prednisone, folate.
- Hx DVT, hx H. pylori, hx procainamide lupus: no active issues.
- Prevention up to date: colonoscopy 2024 normal, PCV20, Shingrix, flu/COVID done. Labs today.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP higher than his usual today. Says his home cuff has crept up into the 130s over high 80s the past couple months. No headaches, no chest pain, no change in salt or alcohol, still a drink or two a week. Adherent with lisinopril and amlodipine.
Exam: repeat BP similar after 5 minutes seated. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P: BP above goal, mild. Rather than add a drug today, home log twice daily for 2-3 weeks and send it through the portal. BMP and CBC today. If still above goal, will add a third agent.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Date of visit: 07/22/2025

Seropositive RA in sustained low disease activity. Morning hand stiffness under 15 minutes. No recurrence of lupus features.
Current medications: methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg daily, prednisone 5 mg daily, amiodarone 200 mg daily, warfarin per INR, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Exam: no synovitis. Lungs clear.
Plan: continue current regimen. Quarterly CBC and CMP via PCP. Return in 12 months.

documents.body: Sorry this took all summer. Two weeks of readings, mornings and evenings. Mostly 136 to 146 on top, 86 to 92 on the bottom. Feel fine.

documents.body: Thanks, that's helpful. These are consistently above where we want you. Let's go over options in person; the front desk will find you a slot. Come with your cuff so we can check it against ours.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Blood Pressure Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here about BP. Home readings since summer run high 130s to mid 140s over high 80s to low 90s; his cuff matched ours in October. Asymptomatic. Taking lisinopril 20 and amlodipine 5 every day. Salt about the same, alcohol unchanged. No NSAIDs.
No palpitations; AF has not been noticeable to him. No breathlessness, no cough.
BP today 148/92, repeat similar.
Exam: heart regular, rate 60s. Lungs clear. No edema. Calves equal.
A/P
1. HTN above goal on two agents. Adding hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg each morning, and propranolol 20 mg twice daily, which should also help rate control if the AF comes back. Discussed lightheadedness and slow pulse with propranolol on top of amiodarone; check pulse at home, call if under 50 or dizzy. BMP in 2-3 weeks for sodium and potassium, order in.
2. PAF, hx VT: cardiology following, amiodarone and warfarin unchanged. I'll let cardiology know about the propranolol.
3. RA, stable per rheum in July.
Recheck BP in about 6 weeks, sooner by portal with home readings.

documents.title: Your blood test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium, potassium and kidney function are all normal on the new water pill. Keep going with both new medicines and send me some home readings in a few weeks.

events.reason: progressive shortness of breath and dry cough

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Bilateral reticular opacities. No focal consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
Noncontrast CT of the chest. Bilateral reticular opacities. No pleural effusion. No mass or suspicious nodule. No lymphadenopathy. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral reticular opacities, no effusion or mass. In the clinical setting, compatible with drug-induced lung injury.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, inpatient pulmonology service
Admitted: 01/31/2026  Discharged: 02/05/2026

Reason for admission: two weeks of progressive shortness of breath with a dry cough.
History: 62 year old man with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and low-dose prednisone, hypertension, seasonal allergies, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin, history of ventricular tachycardia on amiodarone since 2020, prior drug-induced lupus, prior left leg DVT, prior right quadriceps tendon repair. Propranolol and hydrochlorothiazide were added by his PCP about a month before admission. Never smoker.
Home medications on admission: warfarin per INR, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, amiodarone 200 mg daily, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, prednisone 5 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, propranolol 20 mg twice daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother RA; father hypertension and coronary disease; paternal grandfather atrial fibrillation.

Exam on admission: end-inspiratory crackles at both lung bases.
Imaging: chest X-ray with bilateral reticular opacities; CT chest with bilateral reticular opacities, no effusion or mass.

Hospital course: diagnosed with amiodarone-induced pulmonary toxicity. Amiodarone discontinued. Methotrexate held, since it can also injure the lung, pending rheumatology review. Started prednisone 40 mg daily. Breathing and cough improved over the stay. Cardiology consulted: no replacement antiarrhythmic for now; continue propranolol; warfarin continues, INR to be followed closely by the anticoagulation clinic as amiodarone washes out.

Discharge diagnoses: amiodarone-induced pulmonary toxicity; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; seropositive rheumatoid arthritis; hypertension.
Discharge medications: prednisone 40 mg daily for 4 weeks, then slow taper toward 5 mg over about 3 months per pulmonology; STOP amiodarone; HOLD methotrexate; continue folic acid, warfarin per clinic, lisinopril, amlodipine, propranolol, hydrochlorothiazide.
Follow-up: pulmonology clinic in 6-8 weeks with repeat chest imaging; cardiology; rheumatology; anticoagulation clinic within 1 week; PCP.

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know I was in the hospital last week, Jan 31 to Feb 5. Got really short of breath with a dry cough. They said it was the amiodarone hurting my lungs. They stopped it, stopped my methotrexate for now, and put me on prednisone 40. Breathing a lot better already. I have a lung doctor appointment in March.

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, thank you for telling us, and I'm glad you're breathing better. We haven't received anything from the hospital yet; we'll request the records today. Follow their instructions on the prednisone taper exactly and keep the anticoagulation clinic appointments, since stopping amiodarone changes how warfarin behaves. Call us right away if the breathing gets worse.

Outside rheumatology group
Date of visit: 03/24/2026

Seen after admission for amiodarone pulmonary toxicity. Methotrexate held since discharge. On the prednisone taper set by pulmonology. Joints quiet on the higher steroid dose; no flare.
Allergies: NKDA.
Plan: keep methotrexate held until pulmonology is satisfied the lungs have recovered; will revisit RA therapy then. Continue folic acid for now. CBC and CMP with his next draw.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Bilateral reticular opacities, improved since 01/31/2026. No consolidation or effusion.

documents.title: Pulmonology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonology clinic
Date of visit: 05/12/2026

Follow-up of amiodarone-induced pulmonary toxicity. Off amiodarone since 01/31. Cough has resolved and breathing is much better; back at work. Prednisone taper now at 10 mg daily.
Exam: fewer crackles at the bases than at discharge. Heart regular.
Chest X-ray today: bilateral reticular opacities, improving.
Assessment: amiodarone pulmonary toxicity, improving.
Plan: continue the taper to 5 mg daily over the coming weeks. Amiodarone should not be restarted. Methotrexate to remain held for now; I will discuss with rheumatology after the next visit. Return in 3 months.
Allergies: NKDA.
